title: Review — refund route (acme/shop !142)
preamble:
# Mission: fix the findings you chose on branch refund-route

## Context
- Repo `acme/shop`, branch `refund-route`, reviewed commit `9b1e4c7a2f3d5e6b8c0a1d2e3f4a5b6c7d8e9f01`.
- Scope: `src/routes/refunds.js` and `test/routes/refunds.test.js`. Stay in these files.

## Baseline
- `npm test`: 58 tests green.

## Rules
- Each fix gets a failing test first that reproduces it, then the fix.
- One finding per commit (`fix(refunds): …`).
- Never change an existing test's expected value except where a finding says so.
- Don't push.

If `HEAD` is not `9b1e4c7`, the branch has moved since the review: find code by symbol, not by line number, and tell me what differs.

summary.label: Blockers
points: SE-1: any logged-in user can refund any invoice

summary.label: Not raised
points: med, unsure: the gateway may already reject a refund above the captured amount (CR-4)
outside the diff: src/routes/invoices.js has the same missing ownership check

summary.label: For team-refactor
points: refunds.js and invoices.js each load and authorize an invoice their own way; one loader would do

decisions.title: Any logged-in user can refund any invoice
detail: Scenario: user A posts a refund on user B's invoice id and the gateway pays it out
decisions.why: A missing ownership check on a money-moving route.

options.label: Fix
options.brief:
**What**: check that the invoice belongs to the caller before refunding.
**Where**: `src/routes/refunds.js`, the handler of `POST /invoices/:id/refund`, right after `loadInvoice`.
**How**: first add a test: user B refunds user A's invoice and gets 404 (it gets 200 today, so it fails). Then, if `invoice.customerId !== req.user.id`, return the same 404 as for a missing invoice.
**Leave alone**: the 404 body for a missing invoice.
**Verify**: `npm test`, 58 green plus the new test.
**Commit**: `fix(refunds): refuse refunds on invoices of other customers`

decisions.title: The refund cap ignores earlier refunds
detail: `amount > invoice.paid` compares with the whole paid amount
Scenario: 100 paid, 60 refunded; a second refund of 100 passes the check
decisions.why: Refunds can add up to more than was paid.

options.label: Fix
options.brief:
**What**: cap a refund at what is still refundable.
**Where**: `src/routes/refunds.js`, the `if (amount > invoice.paid)` check.
**How**: first add a test: 100 paid, 60 already refunded, a refund of 50 gets 400 (it gets 200 today, so it fails). Then compare with `invoice.paid - invoice.refunded`.
**Leave alone**: refunding the full paid amount on an untouched invoice must still work.
**Verify**: `npm test`, 58 green plus the new test.
**Commit**: `fix(refunds): cap a refund at paid minus already refunded`

decisions.title: A gateway failure is answered 200
detail: `catch (e) { log.warn(e.message) }` swallows the error and the handler goes on to `res.status(200).json({ ok: true })`
Scenario: the gateway times out; the customer sees "ok" and no money moves
decisions.why: The caller is told the refund worked when it did not.

options.label: Fix
options.brief:
**What**: answer with an error when the gateway call fails.
**Where**: `src/routes/refunds.js`, the `catch` block of the `try` around `gateway.refund`.
**How**: first add a test: the stubbed gateway throws, the response is 502 with `{ error: 'refund failed' }` (it is 200 today, so it fails). Then log with `log.error` and return `res.status(502).json({ error: 'refund failed' })` from the `catch`.
**Leave alone**: the success path.
**Verify**: `npm test`, 58 green plus the new test.
**Commit**: `fix(refunds): answer 502 when the gateway refund fails`

decisions.title: No test for a partial refund
detail: The only test refunds the full paid amount
Neither a partial refund nor a second refund is covered, which is how CR-1 got through
decisions.why: The refund rule has one test and it is the easy case.

options.label: Fix
options.brief:
**What**: add the partial-refund test.
**Where**: `test/routes/refunds.test.js`, next to the full-refund test.
**How**: add `refunds part of the paid amount`: seed an invoice with `paid: 100, refunded: 0`, stub the gateway, post `{ amount: 40 }`, expect 200 and `refunded` equal to 40 after `invoice.reload()`.
**Leave alone**: the full-refund test.
**Verify**: `npm test`, 58 green plus the new test.
**Commit**: `test(refunds): cover a partial refund`

decisions.title: `data` names a refund receipt
decisions.detail: The rest of the codebase calls a gateway result by what it is (`charge`, `payout`); `data` says nothing.

options.label: Fix
options.brief:
**What**: rename `data` to `receipt`.
**Where**: `src/routes/refunds.js`, its declaration (`const data = await gateway.refund(`) and its one use, `data.id`.
**Verify**: `npm test`, all green.
**Commit**: `refactor(refunds): rename data to receipt`

decisions.title: `amount` may be a string
detail: `req.body.amount` is compared with `invoice.paid` without a cast
Declined by the reviewer: false positive, `validateRefund` already coerces it to a number
decisions.why: Looked like a string comparison; the validator middleware prevents it.

options.label: Fix
options.brief:
**What**: cast `amount` to a number.
**Where**: `src/routes/refunds.js`, `const amount = req.body.amount`.
**How**: wrap it in `Number(...)`.
**Verify**: `npm test`, all green.
**Commit**: `fix(refunds): cast amount to a number`
